display_url_note: CDN URL - expires after few hours/days
combined_text:
Last month, Invest Newark CEO Marcus Randolph joined a panel hosted by the Newark Regional Business Partnership called the Regional Economic Outlook for 2026 -  Arts, Culture and the Economy. The discussion looked at how arts, entertainment, sports, and hospitality continue to shape growth in the Greater Newark region. Panelists talked about how these areas are boosting tourism, bringing in new investment, creating jobs, and opening more opportunities for local businesses.

description: A day honoring artist Aminah Robinson and reflecting on her life, legacy, and art. Enjoy a day filled with the ultimate kickback vibes. Get lost in art as we spend the day honoring artist Aminah Robinson and reflecting on her life and art that often revolved around the theme of home. Try making your own hogmawg, a clay-like mixture she made to create her sculptures, or enjoy a story reading of one of her books. Bask in the harmonies of vocalist @lyndastarrmusic & her band during a live jam session while journeying back to your youth with an option to partake in a Double Dutch performance by @floydsdoubledutchelite . It’s a day to celebrate community, artistic expression, and our newest special exhibition,Aminah Robinson: Journeys Home, A Visual Memoir.

Our strip woven textile from the Arts of Global Africa collection has traveled to the Brooklyn Museum! ✨ 

Strip weaving is a vibrant art form in West Africa. This stunning piece was created by the Bobo people, one of the largest ethnic groups in Burkina Faso. Weavers throughout the region use this traditional method—working on horizontal looms with foot pedals to craft long, narrow bands of cloth that are then sewn together to create wrappers, gowns, blankets, and more.

Our strip woven textile from the Arts of Global Africa collection has traveled to the Brooklyn Museum! ✨ 

Strip weaving is a vibrant art form in West Africa. This stunning piece was created by the Bobo people, one of the largest ethnic groups in Burkina Faso. Weavers throughout the region use this traditional method—working on horizontal looms with foot pedals to craft long, narrow bands of cloth that are then sewn together to create wrappers, gowns, blankets, and more. 

See it on view in Seyd

description: Celebrating the life of Aunt Sabrina on her 60th birthday.
display_url_note: CDN URL - expires after few hours/days
combined_text:
Celebrating the life of one of the most amazing women, in my life.

She raised me like I was her own and modeled what it looks like to have grit with grace. I watched her get up, handle what needed to be handled, hold responsibility, and still find a way to laugh, to love, to keep going.
As I grow into my own Womanhood, I see her fingerprints within my values: the way I pour into others, the way I refuse to fold, the way I believe I can create a life I’m proud of. That didn’t come from nowhere.

COLLIE BUDDZ

There’s a moment every so often in music when the beat drops, the sun leans low, and you’re reminded why reggae carved its way across oceans and into our bones.

Collie Buddz stood in that moment like it was built for him.

Just a man, a riddim, and a crowd that knew they were witnessing a craftsman at work.

Acts may change, but the architects of emotion endure.

Respect due. Flowers given.

After local business owners complained about the negative impact it’s had on business this holiday season, the Hoboken City Council voted 5-4 to temporarily freeze the CLEAR program, the camera-based parking enforcement program, until January 15.

description: John DeCando organized an annual drive to provide free wrapped gift boxes filled with dog or cat food, treats and toys. This year, he built 500 boxes.
display_url_note: CDN URL - expires after few hours/days
combined_text:
John DeCando, the chief animal control officer in Paterson, knows there are people who can’t afford food, let alone a gift, for their dog or cat.

So, DeCando organized an annual drive to provide free wrapped gift boxes filled with dog or cat food, treats and toys. This year, he built 500 boxes. ❤️🎁

“These are people who can’t make ends meet, and my heart goes out to each and every one of them. Their pets are like their family,” DeCando said.
